subject: Urgent: HavenBridge on-prem — sustained throughput regression & elevated 5xxs
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@havenbridge.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: Ariela Soto <ariela.soto@havenbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: [PROD] Private cluster throughput drop — p95 jump & 502s

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp drop in inference throughput on our on-prem cluster at ~07:45 PT this morning. Symptoms: sustained p95 latency from ~150ms -> ~1.2s, throughput down ~60% vs baseline, and a spike of 502/504 responses across multiple services. This is affecting our live search feature and causing customer-visible failures.

I attached a short log extract and a snapshot of the metrics. We've not changed model versions or traffic patterns. Can you confirm if any agent/patch rolled out on the private controller side? We need an initial triage and ETA for mitigation.

- Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering
HavenBridge

Attachments:
- havenbridge-error-sample.log (text/plain)
- metrics-snapshot-20261109.png (image/png)

2) If you can run `journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200` and paste any repeated errors that'd help.

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [PROD] Private cluster throughput drop — p95 jump & 502s

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 08:24 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Daniel — sorry for the disruption. I'm pulling the on-call SREs and will triage immediately.

Initial quick triage from the agent logs Daniel sent: repeated KV cache miss storms and "kvcache: eviction pressure" messages followed by slowdowns in the tokenization worker pool. Also see intermittent grpc UNAVAILABLE to the model backend on 3 of 8 nodes.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now (can be run without a full maintenance window):
- Reduce per-node max_concurrency from 48 -> 24 (low-risk config change), expecting immediate p95 improvement.
- Toggle model-fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant for 10% of traffic to relieve hot shards (we already have a pre-warmed fallback image).
- Restart redwood-agent on the three nodes showing UNAVAILABLE (rolling, with health checks).

I'll prepare a short runbook and a cluster snapshot to share with HavenBridge. If that doesn't return to normal in 30-45 minutes, escalate for a short 2-hour maintenance window and consider increasing reserved threads for hotshard routing.

- Aditya
SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: [PROD] Private cluster throughput drop — HavenBridge — immediate triage notes

Laura / Jonas — looping you in. HavenBridge (strategic private customer, on a multi-year Dedicated + Private bundle) reported a major p95 and throughput regression this morning impacting customer-facing search.

Summary for leadership:
- Impact: ~60% throughput loss, p95 ~1.2s (vs ~150ms) across production cluster; intermittent 502s.
- Preliminary cause: KV cache eviction pressure + grpc UNAVAILABLE on subset of nodes; likely hotshard contention exacerbated by per-node concurrency/kernel scheduling.
- Short-term mitigations being applied by SRE (reducing concurrency, toggling fallback model variant, rolling agent restart).
- Ask: authorization to request a 2-hour maintenance window (customer buy-in needed) and approve a 10% service credit in case of SLA breach. Also advise whether we should pull Jonas in for a kernel/serve runtime priority patch if short-term fixes fail.

I'll keep this thread updated with outcome of initial mitigations.

- Mike

Thanks for the quick escalation. If Aditya's steps don't recover p95 in the next 30-45m we should move to the maintenance window and apply two code-side mitigations we have queued: a runtime change to preemptively compact the KV cache (non-disruptive) and a temporary kernel parameter that improves scheduler fairness for tokenization workers. Both are low-risk and can be rolled back. Laura — please confirm we can move forward with maintenance and approve a customer credit up to the commercial SLA cap (10%).

Also flagging that Legal should be available because the customer CISO (Ariela) called earlier asking about audit logs/high-availability guarantees — we should assign a CD to own postmortem and SLA communication.

Subject: Resolution plan & next steps — HavenBridge private cluster incident (Nov 9)

Daniel — update from today and concrete next steps. Thanks for your patience.

What we did (timeline):
- 08:36: SREs applied immediate mitigations (reduced max_concurrency, toggled pre-warmed fallback variant to 10% of traffic).
- 09:02: Rolling restart of 3 affected nodes completed; observed partial recovery in grpc availability.
- 09:30: p95 improved from ~1.2s -> ~420ms; throughput recovered to ~85% of baseline.
- 11:10: With customer agreement we executed a 90-minute maintenance window to apply runtime KV-cache compaction and temporary kernel scheduler tweak.
- 11:35: Post-change metrics returned p95 -> ~170ms and throughput to ~98% baseline.

Next actions / deliverables:
1) We'll share a full incident runbook & timeline — attached (remediation-runbook-v1.2.pdf) and a sanitized log bundle.
2) Postmortem draft by Friday (assigned to SRE CD: aditya_rao).
3) Offer: we will credit HavenBridge 10% of November consumption prorated per SLA. Naomi, please own commercial comms and credit issuance.
4) Preventive work: prioritize a permanent KV cache compaction improvement and add a hotshard routing guard in our next sprints (target: production-safe patch in 3 weeks). Jonas will own review.

Attachments:
- remediation-runbook-v1.2.pdf (application/pdf)
- metrics-snapshot-20261109.png (image/png)
- havenbridge-error-sample.log (text/plain)

If you want a short 30-min post-incident sync with our engineers and your SREs tomorrow, we can schedule.

Thanks again — we'll keep you closely updated and will share the postmortem when ready.

- Mike
